Hi Olga / Sean,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Two quick follow-ups from our engineering team:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations for streaming vs. standard (sync) endpoints — our payments flow needs single-digit token latency for the first token in ~99% of interactive calls. Can you confirm how Redwood measures TTFT (first byte vs first token) and the SLA you would be willing to commit to for the POC?

2) Sustained throughput per connection — for reconciliation jobs we'll be pushing sustained streams of ~1k–2k tokens/sec for short bursts. We need a clear minimum tokens/sec expectation per connection and behavior when that minimum can't be met.

We attached an updated requirements doc for context. Ideally we'd like an SLA carveout or contractual language for the POC (and an escalation path if we see regressions). Can you propose measurable SLOs + remediation (credits / fallback) we can include in the statement of work?

Attachments: [Attachment: acme_requirements_v2.pdf (pdf)]

Best,
Jordan

Subject: Re: TTFT & sustained tokens carveout — Acme Bank POC

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. I've mapped the questions to what we can commit and what we recommend as a mitigated approach for the POC. High level:

- Measurement definition: Redwood measures TTFT as time-to-first-token (application-level token emitted by the model runtime), not just first TCP/HTTP byte. For telemetry we report p50/p95/p99 and a rolling 24h window for SLA calculations.

- Baseline (hosted): our standard hosted streaming endpoints historically deliver TTFT p95 in the 60–120ms range for small prompts under normal load. We do not normally expose a formal TTFT contractual SLA for free-tier POCs.

- Carveout (proposed for Acme POC):
  * TTFT: p99 <= 250ms measured as first-token emission (24h rolling, measured at ingress edge).
  * Sustained throughput per-connection: minimum 1,200 tokens/sec for sustained bursts up to 30s.
  * Fallback behavior: if we detect TTFT regressions or sustained throughput drops, automatic routing to a prioritized dedicated pool for Acme flows for up to X minutes while we remediate, plus a one-time credit if we fail the monthly SLA.

- Implementation path: two options — (A) Hosted with a prioritized routing policy + workload isolation rules (fast to enable), (B) Dedicated capacity (recommended) with pinned GPUs and token guarantees (higher cost but stronger isolation).

Next steps I propose: we create a short SLA amendment for the POC with the metrics above, run a 2-week canary (telemetry dashboard + alerting), and include a 30-day remediation SLA tied to credits. I attached a suggested metrics workbook and a draft amendment to speed legal review.

Attachments: [Attachment: proposed-carveout-metrics.xlsx (xlsx), Attachment: amendment-draft.docx (docx)]

If that sounds reasonable I can loop in Legal/RevOps to draft the amendment and provide a DocuSign link.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks Olga — this is helpful. A few clarifications before we take this to Procurement:

- Measurement point: when you say "measured at ingress edge" can you confirm whether that's upstream of our VPC peering termination or after TLS termination in Redwood's edge? Our security team needs the exact measurement point for auditability.

- Credit math: can you draft an explicit credit schedule (e.g., failure of monthly p99 TTFT > 250ms = 5% credit of that month's bill; repeated violation escalates) — Procurement will ask for numbers.

- Fallback to smaller model: if we tolerate lower accuracy in exchange for faster TTFT, will Redwood support automatic model downgrade as a fallback? We need documented fallback behavior.

- DocuSign: please send the draft amendment once Legal has a version so we can route it.

On the technical note: "sustained 1.2k tokens/sec" is per-connection; can you confirm limits per dedicated instance and how many simultaneous connections we should plan for?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Jordan
